title: EA Almanac — 1-2 Emerging Independence
purpose: Parent-facing developmental reference; not a tracker or diagnostic tool.

entries.text: Attachment and exploration coexist.
Independence emerges through imitation.
Pointing becomes a social tool.
New words arrive unevenly.
Movement is a primary route to learning.
Object use becomes more purposeful.
Frustration can outpace language.
Separation can be easier with a trusted base.
Parallel play is common.
Routines can support regulation.
Pretend begins to appear.
Everyday chores become interesting.
Comprehension often exceeds expressive language.
They may insist on doing familiar tasks themselves.
Impulse control is immature.
Big feelings can arrive faster than words.
Coordination changes quickly.
Curiosity can override caution.
They watch adult reactions.
They recognize simple social rituals.
Possessiveness may increase.
Gestures become more intentional.
Back-and-forth games are engaging.
Attention is interest-driven.
Repetition is especially attractive.
Affection can be shown toward people and objects.
Boundary-testing is part of learning.
Doing often teaches more than explanation.
One-step directions become useful.
Actions start to connect with consequences.
Self-feeding is also skill practice.
Messiness accompanies new competence.
Transitions may trigger resistance.
Adults help interpret unfamiliar situations.
Awareness of others is emerging.
Communication mixes gestures, sounds, and words.
Simple play can become deeply absorbing.
Familiar songs and books have strong appeal.
Time concepts are extremely limited.
Choices feel powerful.
Dependence and independence can alternate rapidly.
Adults provide much of the regulation.
Limits can trigger upset even when understood.
Children copy adult emotional tone.
Daily life becomes a mental map.
Meaningful context supports language.
Play shifts as abilities appear.
Simple helping becomes possible.
